chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Bukayr, from Durays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic
And most of them do not believe in Allah except that they are associating others (with Him)
He said: It is the shirk of obedience, and it is not the shirk of worship.
And regarding His Words, the Mighty and Majestic
And among men is he who worships Allah on a corner (superficially)
He said: The verse was revealed regarding a man, then it applies to his followers.
Then I said: Every one who establishes anything besides you is from those who worship Allah superficially?
He said: Yes, and it can be purely that.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between shirk of obedience and shirk of worship in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between major idolatry and 'shirk of obedience,' where the majority of believers associate partners with God by following the rulings of scholars or leaders. He further elucidates the concept of worshipping 'on a corner' (al-harf) from Surah al-Hajj, noting that while it often describes a person and their followers, it can also apply to anyone who establishes a religious authority or practice distinct from the Imams, even if it remains pure monotheism.
